evals.prompt: Map the APIs in this FastAPI service. It exposes /users, /orders, and /health, calls Stripe for payments, and reads from Postgres and Redis.
evals.expected_output: An apis.md with created endpoints in a table carrying method, path, handler location and auth, and a separate called section listing Stripe, Postgres, and Redis with call sites.
assertions: The document is written to docs/codebase-map/apis.md
APIs created and APIs called are in separate sections
The created table includes a method, a path, a handler location, and an auth column for each endpoint
Stripe is listed under outbound services with a call site and a purpose
Postgres and Redis are listed as data or messaging clients
The /health endpoint is documented alongside the others

evals.prompt: what endpoints does this thing have
evals.expected_output: A listing of created endpoints with handler locations and auth, plus the outbound calls the service makes.
assertions: Endpoints are listed with their handler locations
Whether each endpoint requires auth is stated
Outbound calls are covered in addition to the endpoints

evals.prompt: Map the API surface. We have an openapi.yaml checked in, just use that.
evals.expected_output: An API map that reads the spec but verifies it against the handlers, reporting any drift between the two.
assertions: The spec is read as the starting point
The spec is checked against the actual route handlers in the code
Any endpoint present in the spec but not the code, or in the code but not the spec, is reported as drift
Outbound calls are still mapped, since the spec does not cover them
